newsitem.title: USA: Xerox unit sold to GE Capital for $450 mln.
newsitem.headline: Xerox unit sold to GE Capital for $450 mln.

text.p: Xerox Corp said it agreed to sell its Talagen Coregis unit to General Electric Co's GE Capital for $375 million in cash and $75 million of debt assumption, or a total sum of $450 million.

Last September, a $2.7 billion deal by Xerox to sell its entire Talagen insurance group, including Coregis, to buyout firm Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co had unraveled, leaving Xerox to shop the parts of Talagen individually.

In Xerox's fourth quarter earnings release Thursday, Chairman and Chief Executive Paul Allaire said he was "encouraged by the strong interest of prospective buyers in the remaining units of Talegen Holdings Inc."
Industry analysts have previously said that Coregis, a professional liability insurer, represented the most attractive piece of Xerox's Talagen insurance group.
Allaire said Xerox expects to have substantially completed sales of the remaining Talegen companies by the end of the year, consistent with its strategy to focus on document processing.

Some of these remaining parts may prove more difficult to sell, especially the Resolution Trust Group, which manages the claims and reinsurance collection on various books of the insurance group's discontinued business. It has minimal premiums because it writes no new business.
Talagen Holdings also includes a workers' compensation business, Industrial Indemnity, and an excess and surplus lines insurer, Westchester Specialty.
